components.title: Short Rows - Automatic Wrap verses Manual Wrap

blocks.title: Lesson 1: Short Rows - Automatic Wrap verses Manual Wrap

components.html:
Here's a bind off that allows you to have complete control over the tension of your bind off. Even if you are an "around-the-gatepegs" fan ... please try this one.
It takes some practice, but it may become your favorite too!

slides.caption: If you are right handed, end your knitting on the right.
Pull out a few (or all) of the needles to hold position and open the latches.
Needles out and latches open ...
Remove the working yarn from the carriage and carefully lay it in the hooks of the needles.

Carefully pull the needles back, keeping the working yarn in the hooks.
Notice that I've put some tension on the working yarn to keep it in the hooks until the next step.

"Hand knit" each stitch loosely.
This takes PRACTICE, not too tight, not too loose ... .just right!
The size of the hand knit stitches depends on your yarn and how this bind off edge will be finished.
Continue across the entire bind off edge.  The idea is to keep the hand-formed stitches uniform and under control.
Break the working and and carefully pull all the needles out again.
Working from the right, with the latch tool, carefully pull stitch through stitch to bind off.
Work across the bind off edge, being careful not to drop any stitches on the left.
Pull the tail of yarn through the last stitch.
The result: A nice chained edge that is stretchy and just right!

blocks.title: Lesson 5: Neckline Shaping and the Row counter

components.html: Add a design element to the edges of your V-neckline with decorative decreases.  They may take a little more time .... but are so worth the effort!

Jump in!
Following your pattern, knit one side of a V-Neck Cardigan.
Use any shaping method you know ... or try a new-to-you technique for the decreases.
Don't forget, work decreases AT LEAST one stitch from the edge to maintain a seaming stitch for your band or edge finish.
For practice, knit a second sample piece, reversing the shaping. (Knit a left and right cardigan sample). We will be using these samples to discuss finishing later.
For a challenge, knit a sample piece in a stitch pattern or fairisle. Patterning is outside the scope of this course, but this is a great opportunity to hone your skills before working on a garment.

components.title: Take it one step at a time ... V-necks are fun!

components.html:
Use your practice pattern and knit a practice V-neck (both sides) We suggest you knit your first V neckline without shoulder shaping.
Practice some of the suggested techniques first, then add shoulder shaping later.
Your goal:
  • Get comfortable with shaping necklines one side at a time
  • Experiment with decorative decreases
  • Look at preventing damage to stitches in hold
  1. Cast on with any method according to your pattern (try something new-to-you)
  2. Knit plain to the the shaping instructions
  3. Scrap off 1/2 of the stitches
    SIDE 1:
  4. Reset your row counter
  5. Follow your pattern shaping instructions using a simple decrease AT LEAST 1 stitch in from the edge
  6. When the shaping is complete, scrap off the shoulder stitches
    SIDE 2:
  7. Rehang the stitches of the other (side private side facing)
  8. Remember to position the on the needlebed so the row counter engages
  9. Following your pattern, work your decreases with a different shaping method (at least 1 stitch from the edge)
  10. When complete, scrap off the shoulder stitches
  11. Confirm the number of shoulder stitches match
  12. Compare the shaping methods ... which do you prefer?

blocks.title: Adjusting the depth of a round neckline

slides.caption: Most bodies have some slope to their shoulders.... some more than others.
Putting a square shoulder on a slope can cause fit issues
You'll notice wrinkles near the underarm
Warning! Don't try this at home
If you just make this adjustment on an existing pattern ..... the armhole may be too short AND your sleeves won't fit in the armhole.
If you just make this adjustment on an existing pattern ..... the neckline AND center front will be too long.
A well designed knitting pattern will adjust the shape of the armhole AND the shape of the sleeve cap to accommodate the shaped shoulder.
Use a knitting pattern that already has shaped shoulders.

components.html:
To add shape to the shoulder seam knitting patterns will instruct you:
"bind off" X stitches every other row Y times

But binding off creates "stairsteps" that are not only UGLY, but they are difficult to seam.
The better way to shape your shoulders is to use short rows. You'll knit a smoother edge, seaming is easier (especially if you work it on the machine) and the overall finish of your shoulder seam will be much more professional.

Take time to practice short row shaping (AKA Partial Knitting) for shoulders. Use scrap yarn appropriate for your machine.
Instructions are for standard gauge (mid/bulky gauge).

Knit these samples and put them aside for practice in joining the shoulder seams.
Side 1
  1. Using any method, Cast on 40(20) stitches
    Practice a new-to-you cast on method
  2. Knit 20 (10) rows
  3. Work Shaping:
    1. Set carriage to hold
    2. Carriage on the RIGHT
    3. *Opposite the carriage, pull 10 (5) needles to hold position
    4. Knit to the LEFT, wrap and knit to the RIGHT(knit,wrap,knit)*
    5. Repeat from * to * until there are 10 (5) needles in working position
    6. Cancel hold
    7. Knit 1 row across all needles
    8. Remove stitches on waste yarn, garter bar, or hand knitting needle
Side 2 (reversed shaping)
  1. E-wrap cast on 40(20) stitches
  2. Knit 19 (9) rows
  3. Work Shaping:
    1. Set carriage to hold
    2. Carriage on the LEFT
    3. *Opposite the carriage, pull 10 (5) needles to hold position
    4. Knit to the RIGHT, wrap and knit to the LEFT(knit,wrap,knit)*
    5. Repeat from * to * until there are 10 (5) needles in working position
    6. Cancel hold
    7. Knit 1 row across all needles
    8. Remove stitches on waste yarn, garter bar, or hand knitting needle

Match the short row wrap positions?
Some knitters dislike lining up the wraps when working short rows.
They prefer to stagger the wraps and prevent a bit of bulk on the shoulder seam.
In the yellow example, the wraps are worked every 6 stitches on both front and back shoulder.
In the pink example, the short rows are worked at a different interval for one side - staggering the wraps when the seam is joined.
Are you one of THOSE knitters?

Although the pattern instructions tell you to bind off the shoulder stitches, many knitters will scrap off the shoulder stitches, then join them on the machine. (This is our preferred method of joining shoulders)

Picking up those "teeny-tiny" stitches difficult?
  • Use a highly contrasting color, smooth yarn for your waste yarn
  • You will be picking up the garment yarn loop.(green)
  • All of the white stitches (and loops) will eventually be discarded. Be sure to pick up the GARMENT YARN loops

For a flat seam that is stretchy for shoulders try this:

  1. Knit each shoulder and remove on waste yarn
  2. Right side (public side facing) rehang one shoulder
  3. Push all the stitches behind the latches
  4. Wrong side (private side facing) re-hang the other shoulder stitches IN THE HOOKS of the needles
  5. Pull the stitches in the hooks through the other stitches
  6. Back stitch bind off /work a sewn bind off (see video below) to secure the seam

1. Use the practice shoulder pieces you knit earlier and join them on the machine. Be sure to keep the bind off fairly loose - but not sloppy!
  2. Are you happy with your seam? Would you be proud to show it to your knitting friends?
    If not .... try again! Don't wait to perfect the technique until you are hurrying to finish something or using expensive yarn.

slides.caption: Wok the shallow back neckline in 3 steps. Remove each section on waste yarn.
Short row shape the shoulders and work simple decreases for the neckline edges.
Following your pattern, put the neckline stitches PLUS the shoulder stitches opposite the carriage in hold. Set your carriage to hold.
Begin working the shoulder short row shaping on the armhole edge.
Decrease according to your pattern along the neckline edge
When the shaping of the first side is complete, scrap off the stitches for that side and drop those stitches off the machine.
Put the neckline stitches into working position and scrap them off.
Reset your row counter and begin shaping the other side. Put needles in hold on the armhole edge to shape the shoulder.
Decrease at the neckline edge according to your pattern.
When the shaping is complete, scrap off the work.

Each shoulder is ready to be joined to the front shoulders.
The neckline stitches are ready to be worked into a band or any edge finish of your choice.

blocks.title: Lesson 1: Shallow Back Neck PLUS Shoulder Shaping

components.html:
The key to shaping neckline, armhole and shoulders AT THE SAME TIME is to plan ahead.
Knitting patterns will often use the phase "AT THE SAME TIME". If you aren't paying attention, you may finish knitting the neckline and then realize that you haven't shaped the shoulders. Or you may shape the armholes and not realize that the neckline shaping should have already started.
BEFORE YOU START TO KNIT
  • Read and understand the entire section before starting to knit.
  • Make yourself a row chart.
  • Do whatever it takes to make sure that you knit the correct number of rows and end up with the correct number of stitches for your shoulder seams.
Knit it Now Patterns:
Most Knit it Now Dynamic patterns are designed with 1" shoulder slope. The instructions ARE written AT THE SAME TIME Read ahead for success Watch your row counts

slides.caption:
In this example, the neckline shaping is worked from Row 44 to 68.
The shoulder shaping doesn't start until Row 98
No "Knit at the Same Time" to worry about.

In this example, the V-Neck Shaping is worked form Row 44 to Row 108
AT THE SAME TIME
The shoulder shaping starts on row 98
HEADS UP! The shaping is worked both at the neckline and the shoulder.
This Knit it Now pattern provides a shaping chart. The row counts are on the left and the highlighted rows show where shaping is happening on both edges.

components.html:
NOTE: If you aren't familiar with Japanese Notation ... the point of this exercise is to get you in the habit of planning your shaping before you start to knit.
No matter what style of pattern you follow, chart out the rows that you will be working your shaping.

Translating shaping instructions from hand knitting patterns can be confusing. The trick is to remember that machine knitters knit each side of the neckline separately. Creating a quick sketch will help you ferret out the instructions for one side of the neckline shaping.

1. Determine the total number of stitches before starting the shaping
  2. Determine the number of neckline stitches
  3. Find the number of stitches for each shoulder
  4. Examine the pattern left and right instructions (we will work each side separately)
  5. Sketch out the shaping, noting where shaping is happening AT THE SAME TIME
  6. Assign row counter numbers to the shaping rows

Machine knitting instructions for the example below:
  • Set row counter to 000
  • RC 000: Hold the Center 23 and the left 53 stitches
    Bind off 16 stitches (armhole edge)
  • RC 001: Bind off 3 stitches (neck edge)
  • RC 002: Bind off 16 stitches (armhole edge)
  • RC 003: Bind off 2 stitches (neck edge)
  • RC 004: Bind off 16 stitches (armhole edge)
Repeat for the other shoulder, reversing the shaping.
